declared_purpose: Provide API-key-free web search, rendered page reading, persistent interactive browsing, cookie-banner dismissal, screenshots, file downloads and PDF text extraction. Documented behavior includes open-and-extract, automatic cookie dismissal and caller-facing outputs; specific consent choices and intermediate storage mechanisms are implementation choices (SKILL.md:3-63; README.md:9-26,178-196).

data_operations.operation: Send search queries and pagination data to the selected search engine.
data_operations.source: CLI query and page count; DuckDuckGo response forms.
data_operations.data_scope: Query, configured User-Agent and language headers; Brave/Google offsets; all named inputs from DuckDuckGo's next-page form.
data_operations.condition: Search invocation; DuckDuckGo is the default. Additional pages depend on the requested count and available pagination.

data_operations.operation: Read search-response HTML, extract results and return deduplicated results.
data_operations.data_scope: Result titles, destination URLs and snippets; URL-based deduplication.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory, then stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Successful search responses. This path parses result links without opening their destinations.

data_operations.operation: Open a supplied URL in a one-shot browser.
data_operations.data_scope: Requested URL; configured User-Agent, locale and viewport in the browser context; loaded page content.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requested website and local Chromium context. Additional website-driven requests are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Every read_page.py invocation; browser visibility is optional.

data_operations.operation: Maintain a browser session and perform requested navigation.
data_operations.source: Persistent-browser open, navigate, tab and history commands.
data_operations.data_scope: URLs, live tabs, DOM content and any browser state created during browsing; configurable User-Agent, locale and viewport.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Long-running local Chromium context; navigated websites; configured browser proxy when supplied.
data_operations.condition: open forks the server. State survives individual CLI commands until browser closure; navigation, new tabs and history actions use that context.

data_operations.operation: Exchange browser commands and results through local IPC; maintain control files.
data_operations.source: CLI command arguments and browser-server results.
data_operations.data_scope: URLs, selectors, search strings, form values, JavaScript and returned content; server process identifier.
data_operations.condition: Persistent-browser operation. Commands and results use length-prefixed JSON or text; no application-level client authentication appears in this path.

data_operations.operation: Persist initial page extraction for the parent process, then normally delete the handoff file.
data_operations.source: Initial browser page's extracted title and content.
data_operations.data_scope: Full initial extraction, without the later navigate/extract character cap.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: /tmp/web-pilot-initial.json; parent process; stdout to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Server startup writes the file. The parent polls for it, reads it, deletes it and returns the result. Cleanup is not guaranteed if startup or the parent fails.

data_operations.operation: Read page text locally and return extraction results.
data_operations.data_scope: Page title and selected main-content text, falling back to main-element innerText. Extraction reads the content before applying output truncation.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local browser/script memory, then the caller through stdout or the local socket.
data_operations.condition: One-shot reads and persistent open/navigate/extract/tab-new. One-shot output defaults to 50,000 characters and is configurable; persistent CLI navigate/extract request 50,000. Open and tab-new have no equivalent cap.

data_operations.operation: Search current-page text and inspect links or tab metadata locally.
data_operations.data_scope: Matching lines and line numbers, with at most 50 returned matches; link URLs and text capped at 200 characters per link; tab titles, URLs, indexes and counts.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local process memory and requesting caller through the socket/stdout.
data_operations.condition: Explicit search, links, tab-list/tab-switch or status command. In-page search performs local matching rather than sending the term to a search engine.

data_operations.operation: Click page controls and fill or submit forms.
data_operations.data_scope: Selected control and entered value, including any sensitive information supplied by the caller.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Current page DOM and website event handlers; resulting remote recipients depend on the page. Status and errors return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Explicit click/fill commands. fill presses Enter only with submit enabled; page scripts may also react to ordinary interaction.

data_operations.operation: Execute caller-supplied JavaScript and return its result.
data_operations.data_scope: Whatever the supplied code accesses, changes or returns in the page context.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Current page JavaScript context; result or error returns to the caller. Further recipients and storage depend on the code.
data_operations.condition: Explicit eval command; the packaged implementation imposes no read-only restriction on that code.

data_operations.operation: Attempt cookie-banner dismissal by clicking heuristic matches.
data_operations.source: Visible controls in the main document and, if needed, frames.
data_operations.data_scope: Consent/control choice, including Accept all, Allow all and ambiguous accept/agree/continue matches. Actual cookie values or downstream collection are not shown.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Loaded website/frame DOM and click handlers; subsequent server or third-party effects are unknown.
data_operations.condition: Automatic on persistent open/navigate/tab-new and one-shot reads unless --no-dismiss; also available through the explicit dismiss-cookies command.

data_operations.data_scope: Viewport, full page, selected element or selected vertical range; result metadata can include URL, title, selectors and tab index.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller-selected local path, defaulting to /tmp/screenshot.png; metadata returns to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Explicit screenshot command. Final screenshot files have no deletion step in this implementation.

data_operations.operation: Persist and read a full-page intermediate for a range screenshot, then attempt deletion.
data_operations.source: Rendered active page and selected element bounds.
data_operations.data_scope: Entire page image, including pixels outside the requested range; cropped range image.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Temporary PNG from tempfile.mktemp; local Pillow processing; requested final screenshot path.
data_operations.condition: Range screenshot with both selectors found. The temporary file is removed after successful cropping and deletion is attempted after a caught crop error.

data_operations.operation: Export the current page to a local PDF.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Caller-selected local path, defaulting to /tmp/page.pdf; status/path or error returns to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Explicit pdf command; README documents headless operation. No final-PDF deletion step is implemented.

data_operations.operation: Request downloadable content, following redirects and optionally using a proxy.
data_operations.source: Download URL, optional proxy and User-Agent arguments.
data_operations.data_scope: Requested URL and configured request headers; downloaded response bytes.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Requested server, redirect destinations and configured proxy when used; response enters the local downloader.
data_operations.condition: Every download. An SSLError triggers a retry with certificate verification disabled, leaving that retry's peer identity unverified.

data_operations.operation: Derive a filename and persist downloaded bytes.
data_operations.source: Response Content-Disposition/Content-Type, URL path or explicit filename.
data_operations.data_scope: Complete downloaded file; inferred filename and file metadata. Filename inference is metadata processing, not personal-attribute inference.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Computed local filepath under --output by ordinary names, default /tmp/downloads; unsanitized names can alter that boundary. Path, original URL, optional redirect URL and metadata return to the caller.
data_operations.condition: Successful download. Existing paths cause numeric suffixes rather than overwriting. Downloaded files have no deletion step.

data_operations.operation: Read downloaded PDFs locally and return extracted text.
data_operations.data_scope: Text from every PDF page; full joined text and character count.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local pdfplumber or PyPDF2 processing, then stdout to the caller; original PDF remains saved.
data_operations.condition: Content type contains pdf or filename ends in .pdf, and an available parser succeeds. This automatic extraction is explicitly documented.

data_operations.operation: Close browser resources and delete session control files.
data_operations.source: One-shot browser or persistent browser server.
data_operations.data_scope: Live browser resources; persistent-session socket and PID file.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local browser lifecycle and filesystem deletion of /tmp/web-pilot-browser.sock and /tmp/web-pilot-browser.pid.
data_operations.condition: One-shot completion closes its browser. Persistent close exits the command loop and performs cleanup; tab-close closes the selected nonfinal tab. This does not establish deletion of website-held data or requested output files.

potential_excess.data_scope: Permissive consent choices or unrelated actions selected by broad accept/agree/continue heuristics.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Current website/frame click handler; any resulting remote collection or consent persistence is unresolved.
potential_excess.condition: The first matching visible control accepts optional processing or performs an action beyond dismissing a cookie banner.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Automatic banner dismissal is explicit; accepting all cookies and matching controls outside a consent dialog are implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Remove an obstructing banner sufficiently to read or interact with the requested page.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Scope matching to consent dialogs and prefer reject, necessary-only or close controls. Reserve broader consent for an explicit user choice.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Use alternatives that preserve page access. If access requires additional consent, expose that unresolved choice rather than assume acceptance.

potential_excess.data_scope: Full initial page title and extracted content.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Fixed local file /tmp/web-pilot-initial.json, outside the live browser and caller return.
potential_excess.condition: Every successful browser startup writes the extraction; failure before the parent's removal can leave it behind.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Open-and-extract is documented. Disk persistence is a handoff mechanism rather than a required output artifact.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Return the initial extraction to the opening caller while retaining the browser session.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Pass the initial result directly through parent-child IPC and eliminate the page-content handoff file.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve the full documented open response and reliable startup/error signaling. This removes extra persistence, not the required extraction.

potential_excess.data_scope: Page pixels outside the requested screenshot range.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Full-page temporary PNG created by tempfile.mktemp before cropping.
potential_excess.condition: Range screenshot with valid start/end selectors; temporary deletion can be interrupted.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The requested outcome is a range image. README documents full-page capture plus cropping as the chosen implementation.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Produce an accurate screenshot of the selected range.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Keep any required full-page intermediate in memory and persist only the crop; use direct clipped capture where equivalent.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve range boundaries, scaling and rendering accuracy. The excess is extra pixels persisted during a required screenshot action, not a redundant requested screenshot.

potential_excess.data_scope: Downloaded file bytes saved beyond the selected output directory.
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: Local filepath computed by os.path.join(output_dir, filename), potentially outside output_dir.
potential_excess.condition: Without an explicit filename, a server-supplied filename or decoded URL basename contains an absolute path or traversal components, and the resulting location is writable.
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The documented download destination is --output DIR; automatic filename detection does not require a remote source to choose directories.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Save the complete requested file with an inferred filename in the selected directory.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Normalize automatically inferred names to safe basenames and enforce containment within output_dir before writing.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Retain filename detection, fallback names, complete file contents and collision suffixes. Keep intentional caller-selected paths separate from remote filename metadata.

unknowns: Actual queries, URLs, form values, page contents and downloaded documents are unspecified; their sensitivity cannot be determined.

Blocking for end-to-end disclosure conclusions: website/frame scripts, consent handlers and caller-supplied JavaScript are not supplied. Their downstream recipients, tracking, inferred attributes, persistence and deletion remain unresolved.
Search-engine retention and the contents or necessity of DuckDuckGo-provided pagination fields are undocumented.
Redirect destinations, actual proxy visibility and the identity of a peer reached through the unverified TLS retry depend on runtime inputs and external behavior.
Socket/file accessibility depends on operating-system permissions and umask. The source does not establish which other local processes can access session commands or temporary content.
Dependency-managed browser caches, temporary profiles and their cleanup are not documented by the supplied source. Browser closure does not prove erasure of those artifacts.

No runtime evidence establishes whether failure or interruption leaves the initial handoff file, screenshot intermediate, control files or browser process behind. System cleanup and final-output retention policies are unspecified.
